I have been writing about the prostitution of science for decades.

From 25 years ago, this month

See

Media Alert: Watch for New NIDA Study Claiming Animal Tests Prove Marijuana Is Addictive. Great Marketing of Prohibitionist Propaganda.

And

As Predicted, NIDA Buys Its Press Release: " Marijuana has as much potential for abuse as cocaine and heroin."

 

So,  I thought that nothing could shock me anymore. Wrong!

 

This week there was a story that got maximum coverage.

See

Nearly half of drivers killed in crashes had THC in their blood

Then, “THC-impaired driving deaths are soaring, and legalization hasn’t slowed the trend.”

 

From The American College of Surgeons

“Summary: Over 40% of fatal crash victims had THC levels far above legal limits, showing cannabis use before driving remains widespread. The rate didn’t drop after legalization, suggesting policy changes haven’t altered risky habits. Experts warn that the lack of public awareness around marijuana’s dangers behind the wheel is putting lives at risk.”

 

To be fair, they did report that legalization did not increase the incidence of driving while under the influence of cannabis. But how did they report that?

 

“THC-impaired driving deaths are soaring, and legalization hasn’t slowed the trend.”

There is no evidence presented that shows “THC-impaired driving deaths are soaring.”

In fact, it says that it didn’t increase after legislation.”

Did they read their own report?

 

“The research highlights a significant and persistent public health risk that is unchanged by the legalization of recreational cannabis, the authors said.”

 

Was legalization expected to slow some nonexistent trend toward driving stoned? I missed that memo.

 

Now, in the coda the author’s bias is clear

“The messaging over the last few years has been just the push towards recreational legalization," Dr. Ekeh noted. "The problem is that from a public health standpoint, there has not been enough emphasis on some of the downsides and the dangers that can occur. People should treat smoking marijuana just like they treat alcohol: don't smoke and drive."

 

That is the ONLY MENTION of alcohol in the article. Did any of those stoned drivers have any alcohol show up in their blood tests. Writing about automobile accidents without mentioning alcohol might make sense in Afghanistan, but not in Ohio.

 

And what about other drugs, legal or otherwise?

 

In any case, it is not as though there hadn’t been any research on cannabis and driving. If these other studies are defective, then refute them, but don’t pretend that you are adding anything to the discussion with something as silly as this.

 

How sad it is that the American College of Surgeons would print such a blatant piece of Prohibitionist propaganda. At least. the article could have looked at the effect of combination of alcohol, other drugs and cannabis.
